narrativeReportMd:
# Population R4 to R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
`Population` is present in R4 as a concrete draft complex-type datatype and is absent from the R6 ballot core package. This is a hard breaking change for R4 artifacts, code generators, validators, and serializers that expect a `Population` datatype or inline `Population` elements.

## Scope
The analysis covers the `Population` StructureDefinition itself and its local elements: `age[x]`, `gender`, `race`, and `physiologicalCondition`. Inherited `BackboneElement` and `Element` content is out of scope. The R4 medicinal product resources that used `Population` and the R6 `ClinicalUseDefinition.population -> Group` pattern were inspected only to understand likely replacement and migration impact.

## Main migration themes
The main issue is not a same-element tightening; it is identity removal. R4 represented population criteria as an inline reusable datatype with four specific optional demographic/condition fields. R6 no longer defines that datatype and appears to use references to `Group` for the comparable clinical-use population concept. That changes validation, generated classes, JSON shape, lifecycle, and reference resolution.

## Highest-impact findings
The R6 package has no `Population` StructureDefinition, no index entry for the Population canonical/type, and no element typed as `Population`. R4 instances that rely on inline `Population` cannot validate against an R6 model by retaining the same shape. The likely replacement, `Reference(Group)`, is broader but not a lossless mechanical rename.

## Findings requiring human review
Human review is most important for migration mapping. Mapping `Population.age[x]`, `gender`, `race`, and `physiologicalCondition` into `Group.characteristic` requires choosing characteristic codes, deciding whether criteria are inclusive or exclusive, and determining whether the resulting Group should be contained, bundled, or separately managed.

## Backward-compatible design observations
Because R4 `Population` was draft and narrow, replacement by a richer `Group`-based model may be justified. A less disruptive option would have been to keep a deprecated or compatibility `Population` datatype, or to define an explicit cross-version extension/map. No authoritative rationale or map was present in the local inputs.

## Follow-up analysis
The resource-level reports for the R4 medicinal product resources and the R6 `ClinicalUseDefinition` and `Group` reports should own their own model changes. A ConceptMap or structural map would materially improve confidence for automated migration.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: `Population` was removed as a standalone datatype in the inspected R6 ballot package. The top concerns are loss of the canonical datatype, removal of the inline age/gender/race/physiological-condition shape, and non-lossless migration to the likely `Reference(Group)` pattern. The main uncertainty is whether official migration guidance defines a preferred mapping.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Migration is primarily a structural redesign: inline R4 `Population` objects must be removed or transformed into a referenced or contained `Group` representation in the surrounding R6 resource model. Code generated from R4 will lose a concrete `Population` class. Validators will reject the old type because there is no R6 StructureDefinition for it. Round-tripping from R6 back to R4 is risky because `Group.characteristic` can express more criteria and metadata than the four R4 `Population` fields.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high that the R6 core package supplied for analysis does not define `Population`; this was checked by file existence, package index, and type-usage searches. Confidence is medium for the replacement analysis because `ClinicalUseDefinition.population` and `Group.characteristic` are strong local evidence of a likely replacement pattern, but no official diff, concept map, or narrative migration page was used.

oldState.narrativeMd: The R4 package contains `StructureDefinition-Population.json` with canonical URL `http://hl7.org/fhir/StructureDefinition/Population`, kind `complex-type`, type `Population`, derivation `specialization`, base `BackboneElement`, and `abstract: false`.

newState.summary: The R6 ballot package has no Population StructureDefinition or package-index entry.
newState.narrativeMd: The assigned R6 path is absent, the R6 package index has no Population entry, and no R6 element in the inspected package is typed as `Population`. The closest related R6 population concept found locally is not this datatype but `ClinicalUseDefinition.population` as `Reference(Group)`.

facts.note: No matching R6 package-index entry was found for this canonical/type.
This is supporting evidence for migration, not a same-identity datatype counterpart.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The old canonical and type name were searched directly in the R6 package index and StructureDefinition type usages. No exact R6 match was found. `ClinicalUseDefinition.population` shares the user-facing short definition from the old medicinal-product population usage but is a resource element with `Reference(Group)`, not a renamed `Population` datatype.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is a direct identity and validation break. A validator, schema generator, or model library using the R6 package has no `Population` StructureDefinition to load. R4 instances using inline `Population` content under the R4 medicinal product resources cannot be made R6-valid by preserving the same datatype identity or JSON shape.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: The datatype captured population applicability for indications, contraindications, and undesirable effects. Incorrect migration could change which patients a product warning or clinical-use statement applies to, but the report did not inspect real-world prevalence.

justification.inferredGoal: Likely consolidation of medicinal-product clinical-use modeling around ClinicalUseDefinition and reusable Group definitions rather than a narrow inline Population datatype.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep `Population` in the R6 core package as a deprecated compatibility datatype while steering new clinical-use modeling to `Group`.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred goal is reasonable: R4 `Population` was a draft, narrow datatype tied to medicinal-product clinical-use criteria, while the R6 `ClinicalUseDefinition.population -> Group` pattern is more general and reusable. The breakage is probably justified because the less-breaking base design is only partial. Retaining the datatype would reduce validator, code generator, and canonical-resolution failures, but it would not by itself make old R4 medicinal-product resource instances valid in R6 after the surrounding model changed. Full compatibility would require preserving obsolete resource/field shapes or parallel representations, with real long-term interoperability cost.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base R6 design could have retained `Population` as a deprecated or compatibility StructureDefinition in the core package, even if new R6 clinical-use elements preferred `Reference(Group)`. That is a real base-design alternative, not merely migration guidance, because R6 validators and generators could still resolve the old canonical/type. Its coverage is incomplete: without also exposing old inline population fields somewhere in the R6 resource model, existing R4 resource instances still need structural migration. Carrying both the legacy datatype and the richer Group model could also leave implementers with two population representations whose relationship is unclear.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: This would preserve type and canonical resolution, but not old resource instance shapes unless R6 also carried duplicate legacy clinical-use fields or resources.

examples.examplesMd: The example is an illustrative R4 resource fragment showing an inline `Population` occurrence. It is not intended to be a complete valid medicinal product resource. The same `population` array shape is not an R6 `Population` datatype instance because the R6 package has no such datatype.

findings.narrativeMd: `Population` disappeared as a datatype identity. This affects more than a single field rename: generated R4 classes, schema validators, FHIRPath expressions, serializers, and conversion code may all reference the canonical datatype or a generated `Population` model. In R6, those references cannot resolve against the core package. Existing R4 data therefore requires a structural migration in the containing resource model rather than a same-name version bump.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4 instance fragment containing inline `Population` content can be valid under R4 medicinal-product definitions, but an R6 validator has no `Population` StructureDefinition and the old R4 medicinal-product elements are not typed as `Population` in R6. This is hard-breaking for R4-to-R6 validation and high risk for generated code. The same-artifact R6-to-R4 direction is not applicable because there is no R6 `Population` artifact to serialize back.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Inventory all generated models, profiles, transforms, and persisted data that mention `Population`. Do not attempt a pure canonical URL update. For clinical-use population criteria, migrate through the surrounding resource changes, likely creating or referencing a `Group` and using `Group.characteristic` for old age, gender, race, and physiological-condition criteria. Test validation with R4 examples, converted R6 examples, and missing/unknown criteria cases.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The change could have been less disruptive if R6 had retained a deprecated `Population` datatype or supplied a formal compatibility extension/map. That alternative would let old data remain structurally valid while signaling that new implementations should prefer `Group`. The tradeoff is additional legacy complexity in a ballot build that may have intentionally consolidated a draft medicinal-product model.

oldState.narrativeMd: `Population.age[x]` is `0..1` with `Range` or `CodeableConcept`. `Population.gender`, `Population.race`, and `Population.physiologicalCondition` are each `0..1 CodeableConcept`. All four are local R4 `Population` differential elements and summary elements.

newState.summary: No same datatype fields exist in R6; the likely replacement path uses ClinicalUseDefinition.population references to Group resources.
newState.narrativeMd: In the inspected R6 package, `ClinicalUseDefinition.population` is `0..* Reference(Group)`. `Group.characteristic` then models criteria using mandatory `code`, mandatory `value[x]`, mandatory `exclude`, and additional metadata such as method, formula, determiner, offset, instances, duration, and timing.

facts.newValue: Group.characteristic code/value/exclude entries and optional metadata
facts.note: This is more expressive but not a one-to-one rename.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The likely replacement is inferred from local R6 definitions: `ClinicalUseDefinition.population` has the same short/definition text used by the R4 medicinal-product population elements but now points to `Group`. Because no official map was available, the match is medium confidence and should be treated as migration guidance rather than a guaranteed normative rename.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 inline fields are removed with the datatype, so same-shape R4 content cannot validate in R6. The likely R6 representation is also not cleanly representable in R4: a referenced `Group` can include multiple characteristics, exclusion semantics, formulas, references, expressions, timing, and lifecycle metadata that do not fit the four R4 `Population` fields. Codegen impact is high because an inline object becomes a reference to a resource with its own required elements.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Population criteria affect applicability of indications, contraindications, and undesirable effects. A lossy or incorrectly coded transformation could alter clinical-use semantics, especially for exclusions or complex group definitions.

justification.inferredGoal: Represent populations using the general Group resource so criteria can be reused, referenced, and expressed more richly than the four R4 fields.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Add a base R6 compatibility backbone or choice that preserves the four old inline criteria while also allowing the preferred `Reference(Group)` representation.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 goal appears reasonable because `Group.characteristic` can represent reusable, referenced, and richer population criteria, including coded traits, ranges, expressions, and explicit inclusion or exclusion. A field-preserving base design could avoid breaking simple R4 `age[x]`, `gender`, `race`, and `physiologicalCondition` cases, but only by retaining a narrow parallel representation next to the general Group model. Those duplicate semantics are material: systems could disagree about whether the inline fields or referenced Group is authoritative, and the old fields cannot express important R6 Group cases.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking base design would have made the R6 population surface a compatibility choice or transitional backbone, such as allowing either `Reference(Group)` or inline old-style criteria for age, gender, race, and physiological condition. This would preserve many simple R4 instances and reduce transform risk. It is only a partial alternative because it does not cover richer R6 Group content such as exclusion criteria, formulas, expressions, timing, references, or lifecycle metadata. It also risks permanent duplicate representations of the same population facts, validation ambiguity when both are present, and safety/interoperability problems if equivalent criteria are coded differently.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: This would cover common simple R4 criteria, but it duplicates same-resource population semantics and creates validation, authority, and convergence ambiguity.

examples.examplesMd: The examples are illustrative fragments. The R6 example shows why the R6 model can exceed R4 `Population`: references, expressions, and exclusion criteria cannot be represented losslessly in the old four-field datatype.

findings.narrativeMd: The old datatype provided named inline slots for common population demographics and conditions. In R6, the comparable clinical-use population concept appears to be modeled by linking to `Group`, where each criterion is a characteristic with a coded kind, a value, and an inclusion/exclusion flag. This is semantically richer but operationally different: data is no longer merely nested in the containing clinical-use artifact, and implementations must manage references, characteristic coding, and potentially contained or external Group resources.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 content using `ageRange`, `ageCodeableConcept`, `gender`, `race`, or `physiologicalCondition` as fields of `Population` has no same-path R6 destination. R6 content using `Reference(Group)` is not cleanly representable in R4 if the Group contains multiple characteristics, exclusion criteria, formulas, references, expressions, timing, or metadata. Strict parsers and generated classes will see this as both a serialization-shape break and a semantic mapping problem.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For each old `Population`, create or identify a `Group` that represents the same criteria. Map `age[x]` to a `Group.characteristic` with an age code and `valueRange` or `valueCodeableConcept`; map `gender`, `race`, and `physiologicalCondition` to separate characteristics with agreed characteristic codes and `exclude: false`. Decide whether the Group is contained, bundled, or independently persisted. Test for multiple populations, missing fields, local code systems, and cases where old free-text CodeableConcepts do not map to standardized Group characteristic codes.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A direct field-preserving design could have kept the four R4 elements and added an optional `group` reference, allowing gradual migration. That would have avoided hard shape breaks for simple criteria but would have duplicated semantics and failed to force convergence on the more general Group model. Given the old datatype's draft status and narrow scope, a richer replacement is understandable, but the lack of a computable map makes migration riskier than necessary.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: The replacement relationship is inferred, not proven by an official map. Reviewers should verify ballot narrative or HL7 change notes before treating `ClinicalUseDefinition.population -> Group` as the complete intended replacement for every R4 `Population` use.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: R4 `Population` local elements have no terminology bindings in the StructureDefinition. Any coding choices needed for `Group.characteristic.code` belong to the inferred replacement mapping and are covered as a migration risk, not a direct binding-strength change on `Population`.
No local `Population`-specific invariant was found. Constraints present on id, extension, modifierExtension, and `ele-1` are inherited/base infrastructure and are out of scope for this report.
No fixed value, pattern, or default value was found on the R4 `Population` local elements.
No maxLength, regex, minValue, or maxValue constraints were found on the R4 `Population` local elements.
No local slicing was found on the R4 `Population` fields. Extension slicing is inherited from `Element` and excluded.

R4 `Population` has no local Reference-typed element, so there is no same-element reference target narrowing/widening. The likely R6 replacement introduces `ClinicalUseDefinition.population` as `Reference(Group)`, which is covered as a representation/mapping finding rather than a direct reference-target delta.
The R4 local business elements `age[x]`, `gender`, `race`, and `physiologicalCondition` are not modifiers. Inherited `modifierExtension` behavior is out of scope.
All four R4 local business elements are summary elements. Because the datatype is absent in R6, there is no standalone same-element summary-flag change beyond the element-removal finding.

followUpDependencies.reasonMd: `ClinicalUseDefinition.population` is the closest R6 surface found for the old medicinal-product population concept and should be analyzed in its own resource report for resource-level breaking changes.
Migration from R4 `Population` likely depends on representing criteria as `Group.characteristic`; Group's own R4-to-R6 changes and terminology choices need separate analysis.
These R4 resources used `Population` as `0..*` elements and appear absent under the same names in R6. Their resource-level removals, merges, or replacements are outside this datatype report.
R4 `Population` derives from `BackboneElement`. Any inherited changes to id, extension, modifierExtension, or base constraints should be handled by the base-artifact report.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: No official R4-to-R6 diff, ballot change note, or migration rationale was available in the supplied local inputs. This limits confidence about why `Population` was removed and whether `ClinicalUseDefinition.population -> Group` is the complete intended replacement.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Use official HL7 diff pages, migration notes, Jira/change proposals, or normative narrative for the medicinal-product clinical-use model.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: No ConceptMap or StructureMap was found in the inspected inputs to define how R4 `Population.age[x]`, `gender`, `race`, and `physiologicalCondition` should become R6 `Group.characteristic` entries.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: A computable cross-version map with characteristic-code recommendations and containment/reference guidance would reduce human-review needs.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: The R6 input is a ballot build package marked not for publication. Findings reflect the supplied `6.0.0-ballot4` package and may change before a final R6 release.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Repeat the analysis against the final published R6 core package when available.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: Terminology expansions were not compared. R4 `Population` itself has no local bindings, so this does not affect the core removal finding, but migration through `Group.characteristic.code` may depend on implementation-specific or example-bound value sets.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Compare candidate `Group.characteristic.code` value sets and any implementation-guide bindings used in the migrated clinical-use model.
